What this page is: every style, format and macro the AI agent can write through the Confluence MCP (HTML → ADF converter), built through the API with no manual editing, except one draw.io diagram you imported once (section 9). If something is on this page, the agent can do it. What remains up to you at the end lists what it cannot do, and Converter gotchas lists the quirks found while building it.

Created October 23, 2026 by @Ada Lovelace's agent.

import numpy as np

def kspace_to_image(k: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Inverse 2D FFT with centring."""
    return np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.ifft2(np.fft.ifftshift(k)))

9. Diagrams and embedded content

Two installed apps extend what the agent can put on a page: draw.io (native diagrams) and Macro Pack (renders Mermaid, PlantUML, draw.io XML, HTML, Markdown and LaTeX from source text). With Macro Pack the agent writes the source directly into the page, so it can update the diagram later by itself.

Native draw.io diagram (imported once, embedded by the agent)

The agent drafts the .drawio file locally and checks the rendered preview. You import it once (/draw.io Diagram → Extras → Edit Diagram → paste). After that the agent can embed the diagram on any page, as here:

Converter gotchas

Found while building this page; the agent works around them.

Symptom

Cause

Workaround

Highlighted text is invisible

A bare background-color span also gets a text colour equal to the highlight

Put an explicit text-colour span inside the highlight span

All status lozenges render bold

Bold is the default style

Set data-status-style="subtle" explicitly

Status titled "Purple" lost its text in storage

Title equal to the colour name is dropped

Avoid colour names as lozenge text

Macro Pack LaTeX: "Invalid LaTeX format"

Source needs math delimiters

Wrap formulas in $$…$$ or \[…\]

Macro Pack Markdown tables show as raw pipes

Plain CommonMark, no GitHub table syntax

Write tables as raw HTML inside the Markdown

Macro Pack draw.io: mixed bold and plain text in a label is reordered; canvas is ~900 px tall regardless of diagram size

Beta renderer

One style per label; for final diagrams prefer native draw.io (imported once)

What remains up to you

Capability

Agent via MCP

Detail

Slash-command blocks (/expand, /panel, /tabs, /status, /date, /toc, /layout …)

Yes

Slash commands are editor shortcuts that insert ADF nodes; the agent writes the same nodes directly.

Text colour, highlight, alignment, indent, small text

Yes

Fixed Atlassian palettes in native text. Custom fonts and sizes only inside a Macro Pack HTML block.

Native macros (TOC, children, page properties, excerpt, Jira, content by label, anchors, tabs)

Yes

See section 7.

Child pages, moving pages, comments (footer and inline), mentions

Yes

Mentions send real notifications.

Mermaid, PlantUML, draw.io XML, static HTML/CSS, Markdown, LaTeX

Yes

Through Macro Pack, from source text (section 9). No JavaScript in HTML.

Embedding an existing draw.io diagram

Yes

From any page, by name (section 9).

Creating a native draw.io diagram

Partly

The agent drafts and verifies the file; you import it once. draw.io stores diagrams as plain page attachments (name.drawio + name.drawio.png), so attachment upload (personal API token) could make this fully automatic – untested.

Other third-party macros (Gliffy, Miro …)

Partly

Only by copying the exact parameters of an existing instance.

Uploading attachments, local images, PDFs (viewpdf)

No

The gateway token has no attachment-write scope. Once you upload, the agent can reference the file.

Labels, page restrictions, permissions

No

No MCP tool for these.

Page appearance (full-width page, cover image, title emoji)

No

Page metadata outside the body is not exposed. Individual blocks can still go full-width (breakout).

Deleting pages, whiteboards, databases, templates

No

No tools for these.
